about: Which hallmark of ageing a database term suggests: a hint for the converter, never a hallmark of a card. A term not in a row suggests none.

vocabulary.review: López-Otín C, et al. Hallmarks of aging: An expanding universe. Cell 186(2):243-278 (2023), doi:10.1016/j.cell.2022.11.001

opengenes.terms: Open Genes ageing mechanisms (https://open-genes.com/api/aging-mechanisms), by id

rows.label: nuclear DNA instability
rows.source: López-Otín C, et al. Hallmarks of aging: An expanding universe. Cell 186(2):243-278 (2023), doi:10.1016/j.cell.2022.11.001
rows.basis: damage to nuclear DNA is genomic instability

rows.label: mitochondrial DNA instability
rows.source: López-Otín C, et al. Hallmarks of aging: An expanding universe. Cell 186(2):243-278 (2023), doi:10.1016/j.cell.2022.11.001
rows.basis: the review places mitochondrial DNA damage under genomic instability, beside nuclear DNA; Open Genes names it as the pair of nuclear DNA instability

rows.label: nuclear architecture impairment

rows.source: López-Otín C, et al. Hallmarks of aging: An expanding universe. Cell 186(2):243-278 (2023), doi:10.1016/j.cell.2022.11.001
rows.basis: the same hallmark by name

rows.label: alterations in DNA methylation
rows.source: López-Otín C, et al. Hallmarks of aging: An expanding universe. Cell 186(2):243-278 (2023), doi:10.1016/j.cell.2022.11.001
rows.basis: DNA methylation is one of the epigenetic alterations of the review

not_mapped.label: transposon activity
not_mapped.why: the review names transposable elements with more than one hallmark (genomic instability, epigenetic alterations, inflammation): no one hallmark

not_mapped.label: changes in the extracellular matrix structure
not_mapped.why: the review names no one hallmark for the extracellular matrix

go.terms: Gene Ontology biological process terms, release 2026-09-27; a gene counts under a row when QuickGO maps its annotations to the term (goUsage=slim: is_a, part_of, occurs_in, regulates)
